text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
SpendTime(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SameAge(x, y) ::: x and y are siblings who are the same age.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopBonds(x, y) ::: x develops strong bonds with y.
Luke(x) ::: x is Luke.
Premises:
∀x (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x) → SpendTime(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAge(x, siblings) → Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complain(x) → SameAge(x, siblings)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬DevelopBonds(x, familyMembers)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendTime(x) → ¬LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∧ DevelopBonds(luke, familyMembers) ⊕ ¬((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∨ DevelopBonds(luke, familyMembers)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
Conclusion:
SpendTime(luke) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings.
